root_idea.summary: The root centers on the exposure or uncovering of a thing by removing what covers it.
root_idea.development: From this principle develop the senses of stripping garments or coverings, bare or hairless surfaces, vegetation removed from land, the stripped palm branch, locusts understood as stripping the earth, and related extensions such as clarity, completeness, and separation.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran attests the nominal collective noun جَرَادٌ, conventionally cited as جَرَادٌ.

senses.definition: Locusts; the locust as a collective kind of insect.
senses.usage_conditions: A collective generic noun, applied to locusts generally and to male or female locusts. In the Quran it occurs both for the plague of locusts and in a simile for a scattered multitude.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strip away or consume what is upon a surface; locusts strip a land of its herbage, and deprivation or drought may thereby destroy people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I transitive usage; the object may be vegetation, a surface covering, or, figuratively, people deprived of their means.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be stripped or eaten bare by locusts; said of land or seed-produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive or resultative usage with land and agricultural produce as the affected objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become bare: a place becomes without vegetation, a person loses body hair, or a horse or similar animal has short or fine hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The particular result depends on the subject; the hair-related uses concern a human body or an animal's coat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To develop a skin eruption or abdominal complaint from eating locusts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic Form I use describing effects attributed to eating locusts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strip or divest someone or something of clothing, a covering, a peel, bark, or hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II transitive usage; the removed material may be garments, a coat or covering, or hair from skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render land bare of herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of drought or another agency that leaves the earth without vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prune or trim a tree or plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural usage, synonymous with removing superfluous growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bare or draw a sword from its scabbard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is a sword, understood as being released from its sheath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To detach a company from an army or larger body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A military construction involving the separation of a group for a direction or purpose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To divest a thing of every accessory, adjunct, appendage, or adventitious feature; to reduce it to what is bare or essential.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract extension of physical stripping.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave a writing or the Quran free of signs, additions, and accompanying material; by extension, to recite or present it without attached Jewish or Christian narratives.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction with الكتاب or القرآن, concerning removal of annotations, introductory material, or extraneous stories rather than removal of the text itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To separate cotton from its seeds and loosen it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical textile-processing usage, performed with a cotton gin or bow and mallet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perform the pilgrimage separately from the lesser pilgrimage, or to free the pilgrimage from worldly motives.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with الحجّ or بالحجّ in pilgrimage terminology; the latter interpretation emphasizes devotional detachment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or beg something from a group, with the result that they refuse or give it unwillingly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction with a people or company as the object of the request.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on old, worn-out garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or absolute Form II usage with جُرُود, old garments, as the object or clothing worn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become stripped or bare, or to strip oneself of clothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V reflexive usage, especially with مِنْ and clothing as the thing removed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To emerge from an envelope, husk, or calyx.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a grain ear or flower coming out of its enclosing covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cease boiling and become free of froth or foam.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of expressed juice as it settles and loses its foam.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become alone or apart, detached from other people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form V use describing social separation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To outstrip others and move ahead of them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse separating from the other racers, or of a male animal moving ahead from among females.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To devote oneself exclusively and diligently to an affair, worship, or a task; to exert oneself in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with لِـ, especially in constructions such as تجرّد للأمر and تجرّد للعبادة; the sense emphasizes setting other concerns aside.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive or hasten in going or traveling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with في السير for vigorous or rapid progress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To imitate or affect the appearance of a pilgrim to Mecca.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pilgrimage-related construction with بالحجّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast off or let fall its fur or soft hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of camels shedding their coat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become threadbare, napless, and smooth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a garment or piece of cloth worn until its nap has disappeared.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become extended and prolonged without a pause.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the construction انجرد بنا السير, the journey or march continues at length without stopping.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attack one another with drawn swords.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VIII military construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An old, worn, threadbare garment whose nap has fallen away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of a garment worn until it becomes smooth; the plural جُرُود denotes worn garments.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The pudendum or pudenda; the private parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive anatomical usage, also explained as the awrah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The penis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A more specific anatomical use alongside the broader sense of the private parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shield.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun with no further contextual restriction supplied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A remnant of property or cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive use for what remains of an estate or herd.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wide or spacious tract of land without herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An appellative noun derived from the condition of exposed, vegetationless land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The back, especially in the idiom of being struck or shot on the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Appears in the fixed expression رُمِيَ عَلَى جَرَدِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or open space destitute of herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of land or a plain; feminine and plural forms are also used.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person affected by the cutaneous eruption caused by eating locusts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive adjective describing the affected person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An old, worn piece of rag.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine noun related to the worn-garment sense of جَرْدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The denuded or unclad part of the body; the body considered in its uncovered state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing the appearance or quality of the uncovered body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Plain, level, bare land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical or landscape noun for exposed ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The yard or penis of a horse or other solid-hoofed animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term whose application may be broader than horses according to the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom, an unknown person or thing that carried someone or something away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in ما أدري أي جراد عاره and related variants; this is an idiomatic extension, not the ordinary insect meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A palm branch stripped of its leaves; by dialectal extension, a palm branch more generally, including a dry or long fresh branch.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: While the leaves remain it is called سَعَفَةٌ in the primary distinction; جَرِيدَةٌ is the individual noun of the collective term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tally stick used for keeping accounts by means of notches.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An instrumental extension from the palm stick traditionally used for recording counts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An account book or a register, especially a tax or land-tax register.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A further extension of the tally-stick sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Choice, excellent, and strong; used especially of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival epithet with camels as the attested object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything peeled or pared off from another thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the material removed by peeling or paring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A detachment or company of horsemen separated from the main force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The group may be detached for a particular direction or purpose and may consist exclusively of horsemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The middle of the back of the neck, where it is free from flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A diminutive anatomical term in the expression جُرَيْدَاءُ المَتْنِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who polishes brass vessels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unlucky person who strips away prosperity by his ill fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative personal epithet built on the notion of stripping or removing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A year of drought and severe dryness that destroys or impoverishes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a year or season whose dryness leaves the earth barren.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sect of the Zaydī Shīʿa.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper sectarian name derived from the name of Abū al-Jārūd.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hairless or nearly hairless on the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The masculine adjective is contrasted with أَشْعَرُ, one covered with body hair; its feminine and plural forms are also used.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having short or short, fine hair, especially of a horse or similar animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of an animal's coat and, by extension, of hair on its legs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bare or without hair, as of a check or sandal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of an object whose surface lacks hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bare or barren when applied to a place or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine جَرْدَاءُ is used with land and related landscape nouns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Free of froth, dregs, or clouds; clear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of milk, wine, or the sky according to the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Smooth, including a smooth rock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is attested for a smooth rock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Free of concealed hatred, deceit, dishonesty, or dissimulation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of an untroubled and sincere heart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Complete and free from deficiency; said of a full period of time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a year, month, or day, and in expressions referring to two complete periods.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse that outstrips the others and separates from them by its speed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival noun for a swift racing horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A voracious she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the feminine form as a specialized animal epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare substantive extension recorded for the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant or herb said to indicate places where truffles are found, also described as a leguminous plant with pepper-like grains.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plant name; the doubled and undoubled pronunciations are variant forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man ejected from his property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare passive-participial or adjectival usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bare, naked, or drawn, especially of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sword is understood as drawn from its scabbard or stripped of its covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Divested of every accessory or adventitious feature; bare, sheer, mere, or abstract.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract adjectival use derived from complete removal of additions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bodiless or incorporeal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical philosophical use of the abstracted sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Peeled or pared; divested of its peel, bark, coat, or covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participle describing the result of removing an outer layer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land stripped or affected by locusts; in one usage, land abounding in locusts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial epithet of land; the lexical evidence records both the result of locust feeding and the presence of locusts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man suffering an abdominal complaint from eating locusts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjectival use describing the affected person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse having short and sparse hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of the horse's coat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse sharp or vigorous in pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same horse epithet may emphasize speed or vigorous movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Not free from shyness or bashfulness in appearing before others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiomatic expression مَا أَنْتَ بِمُنْجَرِدِ السِّلْكِ and its variants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Not celebrated or well-known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative interpretation of the same idiomatic expression.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Drought destroys by stripping or deprivation.
Land is eaten or smitten by locusts.
The same passive locust damage applied to seed-produce.
Loss of body hair is covered by the bare/become-hairless sense.
Short or fine animal hair is covered by the same sense.
Skin eruption from eating locusts is grouped with the locust-related ailment.
Stripping garments or removing what covers a thing.
Peeling or removing a coat is the covering-removal branch.
Removing hair from skin is included in stripping a covering.
Detaching a company from an army.
Divesting a thing of accessories or appendages.
Specialized construction concerning a plain or unencumbered Quran.
Performing or purifying the pilgrimage separately.
Asking or begging a group with unwilling response.
Emerging from an envelope or calyx.
Outstripping other horses or moving ahead.
Devotion to an affair and exertion or haste in traveling.
Imitating or affecting the pilgrim's state.
Denuded or unclad part of the body.
The Quran-attested collective noun for locusts.
Idiomatic use meaning carried away by an unknown agent.
Stripped or otherwise specified palm branch.
Individual-noun relation covered by the palm-branch meaning.
Diminutive pointer with no independent meaning.
Occupational noun for a brass polisher.
Application to a bare place or land.
Milk, wine, or sky free of froth, dregs, or clouds.
Heart free of concealed hatred or deceit.
Smooth rock is covered by the smooth sense.
Land affected by or abounding in locusts.
Horse with sparse hair and vigorous pace.
Two attested interpretations of the idiom involving shyness or lack of fame.

cautions: جَرَادٌ is a collective generic noun; the Quranic occurrences denote locusts without requiring a separate singular lexical headword.
The expression جرّدوا القرآن is represented as a broader Classical Arabic construction, not as an additional Quran-attested QAC form group.
